dedupe_keys.name: acs commuting flows us census bureau

description: The American Community Survey asks respondents about their primary workplace; coupling each worker's residence and workplace gives a commuting flow. The Census Bureau produces commuting flow tables every five years from non-overlapping 5-year ACS estimates, starting with 2006-2010, mainly to support the Office of Management and Budget's delineation of metropolitan and micropolitan statistical areas; other flow products appear with special projects. The page is a repository of flow products back to 1990, when flows came from the decennial census; the latest tables listed are the 2016-2020 5-year ACS commuting flows, with earlier 2011-2015 and 2009-2013 tables and county-to-county flows for 2006-2010. Coverage is national, typically county to county. Access: free tables from the Census Bureau website. Caveats: flows are not part of the standard annual ACS products, are survey estimates with sampling error, and describe only the primary workplace of workers. The flows support origin-destination demand for road and public transport network flow models, commuter exposure in hazard studies and accessibility analyses. They complement the National Household Travel Survey and the Freight Analysis Framework catalogued here.
